title: Expectation from the tail

prereqs.why: The tail-sum formula is the expectation identity being applied, and it comes from exchanging a sum with an expectation.
Each tail probability is computed from the independence of the two rolls.

statement:
For a random variable $X$ taking values in $\{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$,

$$\E X = \sum_{n \ge 1} \P(X \ge n).$$

Two fair six-sided dice are rolled independently. Let

$$X = \max(\text{first roll},\ \text{second roll}).$$

Use the formula above to compute $\E X$ exactly.
hints: The sum has only six terms that are not zero, because $\P(X \ge n) = 0$ once $n > 6$.
$\P(X \ge n) = 1 - \P(X \le n-1)$, and $X \le n-1$ means **both** rolls are at most $n-1$.
By independence $\P(\text{both rolls} \le n-1) = \bigl(\tfrac{n-1}{6}\bigr)^2$, so $\P(X \ge n) = 1 - \tfrac{(n-1)^2}{36}$.
Add the six terms for $n = 1$ to $6$. The sum of $(n-1)^2$ over those is $0+1+4+9+16+25$.

payload.prompt: The expected value of the larger of the two rolls.
payload.label: $\E X =$
payload.syntax: A number or a fraction. Arithmetic is fine: 6 - 55/36 is read as 161/36.
